 Log in Royals-Mariners blockbuster: All-Star 3B Garcia traded to Seattle in 6-player swap
 56 minutes ago MLB.com
 Share share-square--:R1qlq: The Royals and Mariners have swung the first blockbuster trade of the offseason, reaching an agreement on a six-player swap that will send All-Star third baseman Maikel Garcia to Seattle in exchange for a package of three Major League pitchers that includes righty Bryce Miller , a source told MLB.com's Daniel Kramer and Mark Feinsand on Wednesday.
 Logan Evans and José A. Ferrer are the other pitchers going back to Kansas City alongside Miller,  while Seattle will also acquire right-hander James McArthur and Minor League reliever L.P. Langevin  in the deal.
 The teams have not confirmed the deal.
 TRADE DETAILS: 
 Mariners get: 3B Maikel Garcia, RHP James McArthur, RHP L.P. Langevin
 Royals get: RHP Bryce Miller, LHP José A. Ferrer, RHP Logan Evans
 Garcia, 26, is under contractual control through 2030 after signing a five-year, $57.5 million extension with Kansas City in 2025 that includes a club option for 2031.

 He earned his first All-Star nod in 2025, finishing the season with a .286/.351/.449 slash line and a career-high 16 home runs in 160 games, good for 5.8 WAR per Baseball Reference. He lost time due to hamstring and hand injuries last season, posting a .715 OPS in 82 games.
 The trade is the culmination of years of speculation that the Mariners would deal from their stockpile of promising young arms to improve their offense. Garcia's arrival will also be a boon to Seattle's infield defense; he won a Gold Glove Award in 2025 and was worth +5 outs above average in 2026 despite playing through injury.
 The Mariners did not have a dedicated third baseman in 2026, with 10 players making at least one start at the hot corner, led by Brendan Donovan (36 starts) and Weston Wilson (30).
 The 28-year-old right-hander Miller is under control for three more years. He is coming off two straight down seasons but had his best numbers in 2024, when he recorded a 2.94 ERA with 171 strikeouts in 31 starts.
 Ferrer is being traded for the second straight offseason after coming to Seattle from the Nationals in December last year. He appeared in 73 games for the Mariners in 2026 and recorded a 4.18 ERA.
